sentences: This bill is part of a package that creates a new accountability system for banks, insurers and superannuation funds.
The package would require those industries to meet higher standards of responsibility and face consequences for failures.
The main bill would start the day after Royal Assent, with banks subject to the regime six months later and insurers and superannuation funds 18 months later.
changes: The bill would amend other Acts to support the new accountability regime.
The package would impose the regime on the banking industry six months after the main bill starts.
The package would impose the regime on the insurance and superannuation industries 18 months after the main bill starts.
New entrants to banking would be subject to the regime from when they become an ADI or non-operating holding company.
New entrants to insurance or superannuation would be subject to the regime from when they become licensed.
summary.affected: Banks, insurers and superannuation funds, and their new entrants.

divisions.question: The majority voted against [amendments](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2023-09-04.229.1) introduced by Tasmanian Senator [Nick McKim](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/nick_mckim) (Greens), which means they failed. The amendments related to civil penalties and indemnities for accountable persons. speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: The Financial Accountability Regime (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2023 was moved, making minor and consequential amendments to Commonwealth laws to support the Financial Accountability Regime and transition from the Banking Executive Accountability Regime, with most changes commencing six months after royal assent.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Bills on financial accountability, financial services compensation, health, national security, education and vocational training were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration. The speaker also remarked that they hoped their next speech would be more interesting.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: The government’s mismanagement of the Financial Accountability Regime bills, including a deal with the Greens that was later reversed, delayed their passage, and it broke promises on tax and superannuation, such as doubling super taxes and taxing unrealised capital gains, while the Levy review on financial advice remains unanswered.
